modules.description: Focuses on learning core vocabulary, key linguistic concepts, and step-by-step practical drills regarding Alphabet & Fingerspelling in Indian Sign Language.

lessons.summary: This is Video Lesson 1 from the CADRRE Sign Language series. It focuses on expanding vocabulary and mastering natural handshapes for Alphabet & Fingerspelling. Students learn to perform, transition, and connect key signs under this thematic skill.
lessons.theory: In this video, Fingerspelling in ISL uses a unique two-handed system. The dominant hand is the 'active' hand, tracing or tapping onto the non-dominant 'base' hand. Keep your base hand stable and at chest level to maintain clear visibility. Key focus: signs for C, D, E. The physical height, orientation of the palm, and minor shoulder movements dictate structural syntax.
practice_instructions: Position: Maintain dominant signing hand active. Base hand steady.
Perform the sign for 'C' cleanly in the center of the signing space.
Transition slowly to 'D' without dropping your wrists.
Repeat the drill 5 times. Practice along with the speed of the presenter.

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: What is the correct hand placement for signing 'C’ in Indian Sign Language?
options: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level
Above head height with an upward sweep
To the extreme left or right boundary of your shoulders
Directly touching the opposite elbow
duolingo_style_questions.correct_answer: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: Match the ISL signs with their English words:
Construct the proper order of signs for: 'I see a C'.
duolingo_style_questions.instruction: Remember that ISL typically uses Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order.

image_spec.description: Vector visual illustrating hand gestures for signing C in ISL.
image_spec.visual_prompt: A clean, minimalist vector line art diagram of two hands forming letters in Indian Sign Language, with subtle motion arrows showing hand transition, flat blue background. Depicting hands forming the 'C' sign explicitly with clear anatomical outlines, optimized for gamified learning.

lessons.theory: In this video, Color signs are often linked to body landmarks or iconic items (e.g., 'Red' points to the lips, 'Black' to the hair). Size/shape modifiers are indicated using spatial classifiers and puffing or squinting facial features. Key focus: signs for Pink, Orange, Big. The physical height, orientation of the palm, and minor shoulder movements dictate structural syntax.
practice_instructions: Position: Maintain dominant signing hand active. Base hand steady.
Perform the sign for 'Pink' cleanly in the center of the signing space.
Transition slowly to 'Orange' without dropping your wrists.
Repeat the drill 5 times. Practice along with the speed of the presenter.

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: What is the correct hand placement for signing 'Pink’ in Indian Sign Language?
options: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level
Above head height with an upward sweep
To the extreme left or right boundary of your shoulders
Directly touching the opposite elbow
duolingo_style_questions.correct_answer: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level

Construct the proper order of signs for: 'I see a Pink'.
duolingo_style_questions.instruction: Remember that ISL typically uses Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order.

lessons.theory: In this video, Pronouns are established by indexing (pointing) to locations in the signing space. Once established, you refer to that spot. WH-questions require furrowed eyebrows and must be placed at the end of the sentence. Key focus: signs for They, We, Who. The physical height, orientation of the palm, and minor shoulder movements dictate structural syntax.
practice_instructions: Position: Maintain dominant signing hand active. Base hand steady.
Perform the sign for 'They' cleanly in the center of the signing space.
Transition slowly to 'We' without dropping your wrists.
Repeat the drill 5 times. Practice along with the speed of the presenter.

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: What is the correct hand placement for signing 'They’ in Indian Sign Language?
options: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level
Above head height with an upward sweep
To the extreme left or right boundary of your shoulders
Directly touching the opposite elbow
duolingo_style_questions.correct_answer: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: Match the ISL signs with their English words:
Construct the proper order of signs for: 'I see a They'.
duolingo_style_questions.instruction: Remember that ISL typically uses Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order.

image_spec.description: Vector visual illustrating hand gestures for signing They in ISL.
image_spec.visual_prompt: Minimalist vector diagram of a person pointing fingers to illustrate spatial indexing and pronouns in sign language, blue accent coloring. Depicting hands forming the 'They' sign explicitly with clear anatomical outlines, optimized for gamified learning.

Key focus: signs for Piano, Law, Police. The physical height, orientation of the palm, and minor shoulder movements dictate structural syntax.
practice_instructions: Position: Maintain dominant signing hand active. Base hand steady.
Perform the sign for 'Piano' cleanly in the center of the signing space.
Transition slowly to 'Law' without dropping your wrists.
Repeat the drill 5 times. Practice along with the speed of the presenter.

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: What is the correct hand placement for signing 'Piano’ in Indian Sign Language?
options: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level
Above head height with an upward sweep
To the extreme left or right boundary of your shoulders
Directly touching the opposite elbow
duolingo_style_questions.correct_answer: In the center of the 3D signing space near chest level

duolingo_style_questions.prompt: Match the ISL signs with their English words:
Construct the proper order of signs for: 'I see a Piano'.
duolingo_style_questions.instruction: Remember that ISL typically uses Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order.
